issues.issue: The preamble says the Agreement is "by and among" and defines the defined terms as sitting in Exhibit I, which is not reproduced with the instrument; the party identifications themselves are definite.

The recital defines "Channels" to include J- and K-Group channels but defines "MHzPops" on capacity "measured post-transition, excluding J and K block spectrum," so the same recital both includes and excludes that spectrum for different purposes.
"Excess capacity" that "may be used for commercial purposes" defines Commercial Spectrum Capacity only by reference to shifting FCC Rules, leaving its quantum indeterminate.

The recital defines Future Spectrum Capacity as capacity "accepted by Clearwire and made subject to an IUA," which must be squared with Section 9.01(2) measuring the Term by Prepaid Royalties "used for accessing Future Spectrum Capacity."

"The bundle of value" and "would not have been executed but for all of the elements of the Total Consideration" is a recital of intent that points toward an entire-consideration/materiality reading not carried into any operative term such as Section 9.02's Event of Default definition.

The recital states Licensee is a shareholder of Clearwire Parent and that Licensee desires Clearwire to have "full access rights," a broader grant than the operative access provisions of Articles I and III confer.

This provision characterises the initial payment as partly non-returnable "consideration for the Option and the ROFR," which is hard to square with Section 2.02's requirement that Licensee refund the entire Prepaid Royalties Balance not applied against executed IUAs.
"Exceeds the value of the Initial Spectrum Capacity" allocates no amount among spectrum, Option, ROFR and advance payment, so the payment's character cannot be determined from the words.

The Access Right Royalties are described by a four-item list introduced by "among other items" and closed by "technology, facilities, equipment and other functionality," leaving the catch-all's reach against the enumerated specifics uncertain.

The Option price is "to be negotiated in good faith based on the fair market value" with only a cap, which is an agreement to agree whose enforceability and content a court would have to construe; "Available" spectrum is likewise left to the unattached Exhibit I.
The provision makes IUA payments reduce the Prepaid Royalties Balance, which interlocks with Section 2.02's refund obligation and Section 9.01's Term clauses (2) and (3) in a way that is circular.

"Substantially Similar" is defined by the garbled phrase "a GSA the covers the same metropolitan are in Puerto Rico," and the price floor of $0.10 sits against the $0.15 cap without saying which governs a required IUA.
The Puerto Rico MFN Right extends twelve months "after the Term," which must be reconciled with Section 9.01's fixed Term and Section 1.02(d)'s automatic lapse of Options at expiration.

The provision says the Puerto Rico Option survives "without regard to the earlier expiration of the Term" and in the next sentence says "[a]ny outstanding Options shall lapse automatically upon the expiration of the Term," an internal contradiction on its face.
The lapse-on-expiration rule is difficult to reconcile with Section 2.02's proviso that the Term is not deemed to have expired while Option periods have not terminated.
"[T]he entity providing each of the Access Right Royalties" is not identified and "such additional agreements as may be required" leaves the Collateral Documents' content open.

The opening carve-out ("unless (1) Licensee has complied with the Section 1.02(b) Option Notice ... and (2) the ROFR Offer does not call for payment of a lower price, or other terms that are more favorable") is a double negative whose scope is genuinely uncertain.

The ROFR's interaction with the Section 1.02(b) Option — which terminates if the parties fail to agree FMV, yet leaves the ROFR alive — could leave the two mechanisms operating on the same Spectrum inconsistently.

The $23,000,000 is payable "upon execution" and applied against IUA amounts, which must be read together with Section 4.01(b)(iii)'s Upfront Royalty delivery and Section 2.02's refund obligation to know what is owed and returnable.

The refund obligation is triggered by expiration of the Term, but Section 9.01(3) makes the Term expire on the date the Prepaid Royalties are returned, so the two provisions are circular; the provision also lets Clearwire extend the Term unilaterally while Section 9.01 forbids extension beyond clauses (2) or (3).

"[T]he full balance of Prepaid Royalties less any portion ... applied against royalties due under fully executed IUAs" leaves unclear whether amounts attributable to the Option and ROFR consideration described in Section 1.01(b) are refundable.

"[C]onsistent with the way the Access Right Royalties are provided by Clearwire to third parties under agreements that provide for ... similar" royalties, and "commercially reasonable best efforts" to "consider" a joint venture, set no measurable standard.

"[T]he same capacity and characteristics as the highest level of premium mass market retail service" and the subjection of the accounts to Clearwire's "then generally applicable Acceptable Use Policy" leave the service level Clearwire owes indeterminate.
"[I]n such locations served by the Clearwire National Platform on a full time basis as Licensee desires for its operations" gives Licensee an undefined scope of use of the Educational Reservation.

"[A]djusted upward every five years proportionate to the growth of the overall data capacity" measured by "average throughput" in a fashion "as shall be agreed by the Parties" is an agreement to agree with no default metric.
The count is "two (2) Cost-Free Educational Accounts per Sector" in a Market Area, while Section 3.03(b) uses "per Cell Site," and neither unit is defined in the text of the instrument.
The subparagraph is mis-numbered "(3)" where the following item is "(ii)," and the Local Channel Ratio denominator ("substantially overlapping GSAs then used to provide service") is imprecise.
"[O]fficially associated with such Educational End User" and "outside of its Educational End User environment" are vague boundaries, softened rather than fixed by the university example.
"[T]he lowest wholesale rate provided by Clearwire to an arms-length third party in such Market Area or other comparable market" turns on the undefined notion of a "comparable market."

The clause refers to "any Licensee requesting the right to resell" although there is a single defined Licensee, and "thirty (30) days after the availability of such services" gives no fixed trigger date.
"Clearwire's cost to acquire such end-user equipment" is undefined as to whether it includes overhead, shipping or volume rebates.
"[R]easonably necessary support made available to Clearwire's commercial customers generally" and "as contemplated by their agreement" (an undefined referent) leave the support obligation unfixed.

"[T]he same degree of access to, and use of, any system capability, service or feature set that is provided to premium third party content providers" depends on the undefined class of "premium" providers.
"[M]ost favored program suppliers" and "equal features and/or service sets" set no ascertainable benchmark for the amount Licensee must pay.

The provision directs that "Clearwire shall comply with the provisions of ARTICLE III to ensure timely access to information about capacity usage," but this provision is itself in Article III and no Article III term addresses capacity-usage information — a broken internal cross-reference.

The unilateral right to "restrict the use of the capabilities and services" where use is "no longer commercially and technically feasible" sits awkwardly with the unqualified Article III access grants in Sections 3.07 and 3.08(a).
"[C]ommercially reasonable best efforts" combines two different standards, and "one ordinary unpaid channel carried on such entity's basic tier" is undefined.

Clearwire's delivery of "the Upfront Royalty provided for in the applicable EBS Spectrum Capacity IUA as reflected on Schedule A" is not obviously the same payment as the $23,000,000 Prepaid Royalties due on execution under Section 2.01.

Subsequent Closings occur "when the Parties reach agreement on the pricing," which depends on the Section 1.02(b) good-faith price negotiation that may never conclude, leaving the closing obligation contingent.
The "No Injunctions or Restraints" condition is a sentence fragment with no operative verb, so whether the absence of an order is a condition (and whose) must be supplied by construction.
This subsection is numbered "(ii)" although the preceding Clearwire-conditions subsection carries the same numeral, an error that obscures which conditions belong to which Party.
The certificate must cover "each Clearwire Affiliate that is a Party hereto," but the preamble identifies only Clearwire and Licensee as Parties.

The Closings occur "by electronic delivery procedure" yet the proviso requires the Initial Closing to "take place at the offices of Davis Wright Tremaine LLP," two inconsistent closing mechanics in one sentence.
"[R]easonable best efforts" to do "all things necessary, proper or advisable" is an undefined standard, and it differs from the "commercially reasonable efforts" used in Section 7.01.
The no-consent representation is qualified by "except as contemplated herein or therein," an open-ended carve-out that swallows the representation's boundary.

The representation excepts "Proceedings of general applicability and those related to market transitions" and also "immaterial claims brought ... in the ordinary course of business," leaving the carve-outs' reach uncertain.

The representation is stacked with qualifiers — "only to the best knowledge," "assuming compliance ... by other parties to a Third Party Agreement," and "complied in all respects" subject to a Material Adverse Effect carve-out — so its actual content is genuinely contestable.

The knowledge qualifier here interacts with Section 8.02, which directs that Damages be measured "without regard to any limitation or qualification as to materiality ... knowledge or similar language" in the representation.
"[B]est knowledge after commercially reasonable investigation" including "all facts which it knew or should have known" is a constructive-knowledge standard with no defined scope of investigation.
Clearwire Parent is made the subject of a representation in an Article given by Clearwire alone, although Clearwire Parent is not a Party under the preamble.
The representation is given by "[e]ach of Clearwire Parent and Clearwire," yet only Clearwire is a Party under the preamble and only Clearwire executes the Agreement.

"[H]as complied in all respects" is immediately qualified "other than where noncompliance would not ... have a Clearwire Material Adverse Effect," leaving the standard of compliance internally at odds.

"[C]ommercially reasonable efforts" is undefined and the clause imposes on each Party efforts to obtain consents "required to be obtained by Clearwire and the Licensee," so which Party bears which consent is unclear.
The notice duty is triggered only by matters "which Licensee determines is reasonably likely to constitute a breach," a subjective trigger the obligated party controls.

The covenant is hedged by "[e]xcept as such qualifications may be affected by this Agreement" and by a proviso excusing loss of an FCC Qualification caused "in whole or in part" by Clearwire, so it is uncertain when a breach can occur at all.

The opening limit that this Section "appl[ies] only to spectrum that has not been subject to an IUA" is difficult to reconcile with the same Section's reference to Clearwire's obligation to meet the substantial service requirement on Licensee's licensed spectrum.

The Section is expressed to apply "only to spectrum that has not been subject to an IUA," yet its final sentence permits Licensee to assign "this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder" to affiliates without consent — a scope mismatch within the provision.
The free affiliate assignment right sits against Section 10.09's reference to "permitted assigns" and against the consent machinery in the earlier sentences of this same Section.

The Parties "agree not to express any contrary view to regulatory agencies or the general public" about FCC compliance, an obligation of uncertain reach against the duty in the first sentence to comply with FCC rules at all times.

Clearwire must pay "all fees and taxes (now existing or hereafter arising) imposed on Licensee as a result of the licensing, regulation or use of Licensee's EBS Spectrum by Clearwire or Licensee," and whether "EBS Spectrum" reaches spectrum not under an IUA and taxes flowing from Licensee's own use is genuinely open.
This broad tax undertaking overlaps and may conflict with Section 10.01, which allocates only sales, use and similar transfer taxes "in connection with the Transactions" to Clearwire.

A covenant "to act in a cooperative manner to preserve the intent of the relationships" and to use "commercially reasonable best efforts to maintain that mutual advantage in accordance with the initial intent of the Parties" states no ascertainable obligation.

Clause (iii) indemnifies for matters "otherwise related to the activities of Clearwire, any of its Affiliates or any of its sublicensees or resellers including, without limitation, damage to health," a catch-all of indeterminate reach against the specific operation-of-equipment and provision-of-service items.

"Damages" is defined to include "statutory or regulatory compliance requirements" and matters "of every kind and description, contingent or otherwise," with no exclusion of consequential loss, so its outer limit is contestable.

The Deductible is stated to apply to liability "under Section 8.01(a)(i) or Section 8.01(b)(i)" — the representation-and-warranty limbs — yet the operative words also speak of "the breach of any covenant," which is indemnified under the (ii) limbs that are not subject to the Deductible.
As drafted the covenant reference here cannot be squared with Sections 8.01(a)(ii) and 8.01(b)(ii), which impose covenant indemnities without any threshold.

The clause preserves the indemnity despite late notice "except to the extent that the indemnifying Party can demonstrate actual loss and prejudice," qualifying the "reasonably and promptly" notice requirement of Section 8.04(a) in a way whose effect must be construed.

Clause (3) makes the Term end when Licensee returns the unused Prepaid Royalties, while Section 2.02 makes that refund due within five days after the Term expires — the two provisions are circular and cannot both be given literal effect; the extension right here also conflicts with Section 2.02's unlimited extension right.
The Term sentence ends with the unexplained qualifier "except as it pertains to Puerto Rico," which identifies no rule for how long the Term runs for Puerto Rico spectrum.

The list of termination events is mis-lettered ("(i)" followed by "(1)" then "(iii)"), and clauses (ii) and (iii) give the two Parties materially different cure periods for the same defined Event of Default.

The direction that on termination "for any cause" the Prepaid Royalties Balance be refunded "as provided in Section 2.02" runs into Section 1.01(b)'s characterisation of part of that payment as consideration for the Option and ROFR.

An "Event of Default" requires failure to perform "a material obligation" in circumstances "where such failure results in the inability of the other party to exercise its full rights," a compound and undefined threshold.
"Loss" is defined only "in the applicable IUA," a document not set out in this instrument, so the trigger for the cooperation duty cannot be read off this Agreement.

Survival of obligations "that by their nature would continue beyond expiration or termination" is an open standard, and the Option/ROFR carve-out extends to events that "would have occurred, if Licensee complied in full."
Indefinite survival of Options and rights of first refusal is hard to reconcile with Section 1.02(d)'s rule that "[a]ny outstanding Options shall lapse automatically upon the expiration of the Term."
The obligation runs to the "Licensee(s) Indemnified Parties," a term defined in Section 8.01(b) as the "Licensee Indemnified Parties," and overlaps Section 7.06's broader fee-and-tax undertaking.

The statement that "[a]ll agreements and covenants contained herein shall survive indefinitely" sits against Section 9.03, which limits survival to obligations that "by their nature would continue beyond expiration or termination."
The entire-agreement statement must be squared with the Agreement's dependence on the IUAs, Collateral Documents and Exhibit I definitions referred to in Sections 1.01(a), 1.03 and the preamble.

Notice is "deemed given when delivered personally or by overnight courier, or mailed by certified mail," so for certified mail the deeming event is dispatch rather than receipt despite the return-receipt requirement; the Kirkland, Washington addressee is also given a 415 area-code facsimile number.
"[T]o the extent possible, allow the other Party reasonable time to comment" sets an unmeasurable qualification on the publicity exception.

The one-sentence severability clause says only that "the balance of this Agreement shall remain in effect," with no reformation or essential-term qualification, so its effect on a failed core term such as the Option pricing would have to be construed.
"[P]ermitted assigns" presupposes an assignment-restriction provision, but the Agreement contains no general anti-assignment clause other than the FCC-license-specific Section 7.04.

The clause both stipulates that "monetary damages alone will not be adequate" and preserves "money damages" as a cumulative remedy, an internal tension a court would have to reconcile before ordering specific performance.
The cumulative-remedies and specific-performance rights sit against Section 10.11, which makes the Dispute Resolution Procedures the Parties' "sole means" of resolving disputes.

The provision states the Dispute Resolution Procedures are the Parties' "sole means" but the sentence is cut off, so the scope of disputes covered and whether resort to court is barred cannot be determined from the words.

A "sole means" dispute procedure cannot easily be squared with Section 10.10's guarantee of specific performance and cumulative remedies "at law or in equity," nor with the ad hoc arbitration references in Sections 1.04 and 3.03(b).
